proposal.utterance: What BFO type fits 'the legal rule enduring relation'?

entities.label: LegalRuleEnduringRelation
entities.rationale: A 'legal rule enduring relation' is the information-like pattern or content that persists across instantiations — the abstract relational structure a rule encodes (e.g., correlative rights-duties, power-liability). This is paradigmatically a Generically Dependent Continuant: it is an information-bearing pattern that can be multiply instantiated in different concrete legal texts or practices, is not tied to a single bearer, and endures as a copyable/shareable structure. It is not a Quality (which inheres in exactly one bearer) nor a Process (which unfolds in time). The closest existing class is working:RelationalStructure (also BFO_0000031); this new class could be a subclass of that.

relations.rationale: LegalRuleEnduringRelation is a more specific kind of RelationalStructure — it is the specific relational pattern encoded by a legal rule that persists across instantiations. Placing it under RelationalStructure (also BFO_0000031) preserves hierarchy and avoids redundancy with existing classes.

open_questions: Do you mean the *abstract relational content* of a rule (the normative structure it encodes, e.g., a Hohfeldian right-duty correlation) — which fits BFO_0000031 (Generically Dependent Continuant)? Or do you mean the *ongoing social practice* of actors treating each other in accordance with a rule — which would fit BFO_0000015 (Process) or BFO_0000019 (Quality)? Or the *disposition* of a legal institution to persist in enforcing a relational norm — which fits BFO_0000016 (Disposition)?
Should this be a subclass of the existing working:RelationalStructure, or do you want it at the same level as a sibling?

Is 'enduring relation' meant to highlight temporal persistence (in which case InstitutionalPersistence as a co-instantiated Quality may also be relevant), or is it purely about the relational/structural content of the rule?
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'legal rule enduring relation' most naturally picks out the abstract relational pattern or content encoded by a legal rule — the normative correlative structure (e.g., right/duty, power/liability) that persists independently of any particular physical inscription and can be shared across many instantiations. This fits BFO_0000031 (Generically Dependent Continuant), which covers information-like entities that depend generically (not specifically) on bearers and can be copied or multiply instantiated. The proposed class LegalRuleEnduringRelation is typed as BFO_0000031 and placed as a subclass of the existing working:RelationalStructure for consistency with the ontology's prior commitments. However, if the user intends the temporal persistence aspect as primary (an ongoing quality of a rule), BFO_0000019 (Quality) would be defensible, and existing class working:InstitutionalPersistence would be nearby. If the user intends the *practice* of relational enforcement, BFO_0000015 (Process) applies. Open questions are raised to resolve this ambiguity before committing.
